name: T-90M 'Proryv'

placement_rationale.text: T-90M is Russia's most modern MBT actually fielded at scale, with a 125mm gun, Relikt ERA and Shtora-1 soft-kill APS — protection built for a direct-fire posture close to the line. 3 km sits toward the close end of doctrine.md's lower-sky bracket (1–1.5 km with local air/drone superiority, ~7 km without), plausible for a modern tank but tempered by the asset's own contrast_vs_traditional note: photographed with improvised slat 'cope cage' armor, evidence that factory protection alone hasn't been enough to hold the closest positions safely.

cost.display: ~$4.5M per unit (destroyed-unit valuation reported by Euromaidan Press)

key_facts.label: Main armament
key_facts.value: 125mm smoothbore + Relikt ERA + Shtora-1 soft-kill APS

key_facts.label: Spec
key_facts.value: combines T-72 chassis with upgraded T-80-derived turret systems

characteristics: 125mm smoothbore + Relikt ERA + Shtora-1 soft-kill APS
combines T-72 chassis with upgraded T-80-derived turret systems
Strength: Russia's most modern tank actually fielded at scale (T-14 Armata is not); improved crew protection over base T-72/T-90

Limitation: Only ~67 in active service at war's start — by Dec 2024 open-source tracking (Oryx) had already confirmed 100 losses, i.e. more losses than the starting fleet, meaning most in service now are wartime production
Estimated quantity available: ~200 in active service by late 2025 per Janes reporting (grown from ~50 in 2022 via wartime production, ~150-250/yr claimed production rate)
employment_notes: Billed by Russian officials as 'the best tank in the world' pre-war; loss count exceeding starting inventory is one of the starkest illustrations of attrition-vs-modernization tension in this war
contrast_vs_traditional: Russia's most modern fielded MBT still gets photographed with welded-on "cope cage" slat armor over the turret — an improvised, crew-level answer to top-attack drone strikes that the factory-armor doctrine behind the T-90M never accounted for. It is a concrete illustration of the doctrine.md finding that FPV saturation, not frontal armor class, now sets survivability at the front.

notes: Specs meet the bar but the unit cost is an estimate — cost is not verified.
